newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBS SEEN EASING TO LOWER END OF 126-127.
newsitem.headline: JGBS SEEN EASING TO LOWER END OF 126-127.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract's range is likely to ease to the lower end of 126-127 on Wednesday after the topside proved heavy earlier this week, traders said.
Weak Dow industrials overnight may drag down Tokyo's Nikkei stock index below 19,000 again after Tuesday's brief recovery. But that is unlikely to give a boost to the September contract, they said.
"The market may remain dull even if share prices fall today. We saw the September fail to rally on the Nikkei's drop below 19,000 yen on Monday," said a brokerage house dealer.
The September closed at its session low of 126.41 on Tuesday. Its close on LIFFE was even lower at 126.38.

Traders said sentiment had been weakening since Monday, when the September contract failed to break above a recent high of 126.91 despite the Nikkei's sharp fall by nearly four percent to 18,824.18. That was mainly due to a lack of cash bond buying from investors, they said.
The focus is on U.S. price data later on Wednesday, as no domestic economic data is due during the day, traders said.
"JGB trade may revive if fears of a U.S. rate hike hurt U.S. Treasuries," said a dealer at trust bank securities unit.
